title: What if Everest sat at the bottom of the ocean? #shorts
description:
What if Mount Everest sat on the floor of the Mariana Trench? Its summit would still be about two kilometres underwater: Challenger Deep is estimated at 10,935 m, Everest is 8,848.86 m tall, leaving about 2,086 m of water.

Numbers: 10,935 m - 8,848.86 m = 2,086 m. Depth estimates of Challenger Deep vary by tens of metres between surveys (about 10,900 to 11,000 m). The Kola Superdeep Borehole, 12,262 m, is deeper than the trench is deep.

Sources:
- NOAA estimate of Challenger Deep depth (Greenaway et al. 2021, Deep Sea Research Part I)
- Everest height 8,848.86 m, joint China-Nepal survey 2020
- Kola Superdeep Borehole depth

Narration is a synthetic (AI-generated) voice. Visuals are animated graphics and Wikimedia Commons images.

scenes.say: The deepest spot in the sea, Challenger Deep, is about ten thousand, nine hundred and thirty-five metres down, says NOAA.
Everest stands eight thousand, eight hundred and forty-nine metres tall.
Put its base on the trench floor, and its summit would sit about two thousand metres below the surface.
That is two kilometres of open water above the tallest mountain on Earth.
Depth estimates vary by tens of metres, but the conclusion holds.

show.text: Estimates vary by tens of metres. The *conclusion* doesn't.

scenes.say: And humans have drilled even deeper into rock. The Kola borehole reached twelve point two six two kilometres.
Follow for the next impossible what-if.
